scope: Two user-supplied Air Quality Division On-Site Inspection PDFs were reread from page 1 through the final page, rendered for visual verification, hash-matched against the published Wexford library, and reconciled without duplicate publication.
method: Read every page in order with pypdf text extraction and checked the rendered page image for headings, tables, section transitions, footer marks and legibility.
Native text was present and coherent on all seven pages; no page required OCR. The page images were used to verify the extracted reading rather than treating extraction alone as page review.
Compared byte length, SHA-256, page count and substantive identity with the canonical Wexford assets and the existing N3862 catalog records.

Classified statements as inspection observations, reported facility statements, permit requirements or agency conclusions; no PFAS, WWTP-receiving or final-load conclusion was inferred from these air-program records.

findings.finding: The 2015 inspection reports a scheduled air-permit inspection under MI-ROP-N3862-2012, with no downwind odors, projected NMOC below the 50-Mg/year threshold, no recent landfill expansion, and an agency conclusion of compliance with applicable air permitting at the visit.
findings.boundary: This is an air-permitting record, not a PFAS analytical result, WWTP receiving log, leachate ticket or proof of a final Cadillac delivery.

findings.finding: The 2017 inspection reports a 3.45-million-Mg landfill design capacity, active gas collection and flare, post-closure aeration ponds for contaminated-groundwater remediation, and a Rule 285(aa)-exempt leachate evaporation system; it reports 31.04 Mg NMOC for 2017 from March 2016 Tier 2/LandGEM work and concludes applicable air permitting was compliant at the inspection.
findings.boundary: The leachate evaporation statement is operational air-program context. It does not establish when Cadillac stopped receiving Wexford leachate, whether every load was evaporated, or the final truck/load date.

findings.finding: Both inspections say asbestos shipment records were maintained with generator, transporter, quantity, packaging/coverage and receipt-date information and that no discrepancies were noted.
findings.boundary: The underlying shipment records are not attached to these PDFs and are not leachate-to-WWTP tickets.

leadTrace.lead: The 2017 air inspection references an exempt leachate evaporation system and post-closure groundwater-remediation aeration ponds.
leadTrace.targetRecord: N3862 air-permit and groundwater/remediation records in Category 12, including the existing N3862 staff-report and permit family
leadTrace.tieBack: Use as operational context when reading the landfill injection/groundwater and leachate records; it does not close the WWTP final-load question.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: These inspection pages do not identify a Cadillac receiving date, volume, transporter, ticket or invoice.

leadTrace.targetRecord: Existing N3862 compliance/violation records in Category 08 and Category 12
leadTrace.tieBack: Cross-reference the violation-notice series for reporting history; do not treat the reference as a new violation finding.
leadTrace.remainingUncertainty: The inspection PDFs do not identify the notice number or attach the notice.
